en: The Lotus-Eye Dhāraṇī Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Imperial Preceptor and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
under Imperial Edict during the Western Heaven Translation Era.
Namo ratnatrayāya | Nama āryapadmāvatī-tārāyai tathāgatāya | Namo sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhine ||
Nirdeśatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā | oṃ tara tara tiri tiri turu turu kara kara kili kili kuru kuru vara vara bili bili buḥ ||
Rūburuṇaya naya kuru kuru mocaya svāhā | Jvalanāvahini nibhi svāhā | Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna...
Hrīḥ svāhā mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca svāhā. This is the Padmanetra-dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who, at the break of dawn,
reverently makes offerings and recites this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times,
or maintains it with a focused mind for one day, two days, or even up to twenty-one days;
All karmic obstacles and hindrances will be completely eliminated.
Furthermore, one shall suffer no afflictions of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, or body,
and the mind shall not be distracted or deranged.
Furthermore, they attain the fivefold purity of the eyes, the fivefold purity of the nose,
the fivefold purity of the tongue, and the fivefold purity of the mind;
their physical forms are upright and straight, and their minds are free from defilement and stain.
In all successive births, may they constantly resolve upon bodhicitta;
may they always behold the Buddhas together with the assembly of noble ones and hear the sublime Dharma until reaching the site of enlightenment and attaining perfect awakening.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Dharani of the Lotus Eye.
